headline: Medium-risk pair: shared-file and output-chaining pathways can enable prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors; no direct evidence of a tighter coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can ingest runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and reads/writes project files; Agent B reads and writes files in a document pipeline. That creates a plausible shared-file or content-passing bridge where B’s parsed document content could influence A, or A’s outputs could be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred from docs only, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or document directory
IF A consumes file content or MCP payloads without provenance checks
IF B emits text that A later parses as instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable shared clipboard or shared MCP channels
Add provenance tags to B outputs
Review A’s file-ingestion prompts before enabling
requires-engineering: enforce content-type boundaries between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches session history, project code, AGENTS.md, README.md, and provider auth data, while B can read/write filesystem and has network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive material from A can flow into B’s document-processing inputs and then out through B’s allowlisted network path. The profiles do not prove this default, but the pathway is credible enough to rate medium.
conditions: IF A and B share the same filesystem tree
IF A’s session history or auth prompts are stored in files B can read
IF B uploads extracted document contents to its backend
mitigations: Keep A secrets outside B-readable paths
Mount B on a read-only, redacted corpus
Rotate any provider auth data after shared runs
Audit B’s upload destinations
requires-engineering: add automatic secret redaction before B ingestion

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network egress, browser/subprocess spawning, and full-permissions mode requested; B can install packages, write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses. Even without a proven shared directory, their overlapping write-adjacent and process capabilities can conflict if orchestrated together, especially under multiple-instance support. The lack of explicit locking or coordination means the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same host resources
IF either agent modifies shared files or package state
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or per-agent isolation
mitigations: Run agents in separate containers
Use distinct package environments
Block concurrent writes to shared paths
Schedule non-overlapping execution windows
requires-engineering: add resource locks for shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce code/search results and team messages, while B processes documents and can write outputs. If B treats A’s outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade from A’s generated content into B’s downstream artifacts. Because no verification step is documented and both agents have action-capable surfaces, the interaction is plausible in default workflows and merits medium severity.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text or citations as input
IF B writes derived artifacts without human review
IF A’s outputs are not independently verified before use
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B ingestion
Add checksum or citation validation
Keep A as advisory only
Log source provenance in B outputs
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A handles provider auth prompts, installation identifiers, session history, and project code; B processes documents and images and has a privacy-policy endpoint. If regulated or personal data is placed into the shared workflow, differing retention or residency terms could create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction conflict, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through both agents
IF A’s session history or auth prompts are retained longer than B’s document outputs
IF the deployment mixes jurisdictions or retention policies
mitigations: Classify data before routing
Avoid sending regulated data through A
Align retention settings across both tools
Review privacy-policy terms for B
requires-engineering: enforce jurisdiction-aware routing
